summary.text: Abolitionism is the political movement to end slavery and free enslaved people around the world.
It gained momentum in the western world in the late 18th and 19th centuries, with Britain making the slave trade illegal in 1807 and ending slavery in its colonies in 1833.
The United States passed the 13th Amendment in December 1865, and in 1888 Brazil became the last country in the Americas to outlaw slavery.

items.prompt: A classmate says Britain freed every enslaved person in its colonies in 1807. What is the correction?

options.label: That law ended the trade, but people already enslaved waited until 1833
That law freed colonial people, but owners were only paid in 1833
That law freed people in England only, and never touched the colonies
That law freed colonial people, and the trade stayed legal until 1833

items.explain: The 1807 act made the slave trade illegal across the empire, but existing slaves in the colonies were not liberated until the Slavery Abolition Act 1833.

items.prompt: A friend claims the US 13th Amendment ended every kind of forced labor, with no carve-outs. Is that right?

options.label: Yes, it ended every form of compulsory work for everyone
No, it left a gap for people punished for a crime
No, it only freed people living in the southern states
Yes, but it covered only people born after it passed

items.explain: The amendment ended slavery 'except as a punishment for crime'.

items.prompt: Which fact makes Haiti's end of slavery different from the other countries described?

options.label: It was decreed from overseas by a European monarch in 1791
It followed a vote in Parliament to compensate former owners
It came as a result of a revolution that enslaved people themselves fought
It came after neighbouring countries had freed their own people

items.explain: Haiti is described as the first and only country to self-liberate from slavery, through a revolution begun by a slave revolt led by formerly enslaved people.

items.prompt: In the 1920s and 30s an international organization set out to eradicate slavery worldwide. How did it go about it?

options.label: It sent troops to free enslaved people in the countries it named
It raised a shared fund to buy the freedom of enslaved people
It barred ships from countries that still allowed slavery
It set up commissions that investigated slavery and produced treaties

items.explain: The League of Nations founded commissions that conducted international investigations and created treaties such as the 1926 Slavery Convention.

items.prompt: A traveler crosses from the northern US into the southern states in 1805. What difference in the law would they meet?

options.label: Northern states had abolished slavery, while southern states still allowed it
Southern states had abolished slavery, while northern states still allowed it
Both regions had abolished it, but only northern states enforced it
Every state still allowed it except Vermont and Pennsylvania

items.explain: By 1804 the rest of the northern states had abolished slavery, but it remained legal in southern states.

items.prompt: A merchant brings enslaved Africans to a French port to sell them. What happened in a recorded case from the 1500s?

options.label: He sold them freely, because French law allowed it in port towns
He was arrested and the people were freed, as slavery was called intolerable in France
He paid a fine but kept the people and sold them elsewhere
He was allowed to sell them, but only to colonial buyers

items.explain: A Norman merchant who tried to sell slaves in Bordeaux in 1571 was arrested and his slaves were freed.
